title: Constrained-decoder edge-case simulation harness for partial-stream integrity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a repeatable simulation harness that stresses constrained-decoders and the surrounding stream reassembly logic by injecting realistic partial-stream failures, tool-call interleaving, and schema-noise. The goal is to classify failure modes, measure detection/recovery latency, and generate actionable regression signals so Console/Runtime teams can triage and fix root causes before customer incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run 10k synthetic sessions with parameterized failure modes (chunk drop, dropped tokens, token duplication, delimiter corruption) and produce a summary report
For each run the system captures: well-formed-structured-output rate, parser recovery time distribution, incorrect-tool-invocation rate, and mapped failure-mode labels
Integration with tracing: each simulated request includes a trace ID surfaced to Console so devs can correlate failures with runtime traces
Regression alert generation: when well-formed-structured-output rate drops below threshold (default 99.0%), create an automated ticket template and attach a failing example
Playbooks for top 3 failure modes created and linked in the harness report (prefix reassembly, sentinel bleed-through, buffer boundary/kernel mismatch)
testing_plan: Design data generator: produce model outputs that include valid structured payloads, then apply controlled corruptions at chunk boundaries
Parameterize model surface: sequence lengths, tokenization artifacts (byte-level splits), streaming chunk sizes, and interleaved tool-return snippets
Run constrained decoder and a tolerant fallback parser in parallel to compare outcomes and log divergence events
Record per-run telemetry: time-to-first-valid-parse, percentage of partial-recoveries, downstream tool ID mismatches
Expose harness results as artifacts (CSV/JSON) and a lightweight HTML dashboard for quick human review
notes: This harness focuses on the interaction between the streaming layer (runtime), the constrained-decoder, and the tool-calling plumbing. It deliberately avoids model generation quality experiments — synthetic payloads emulate likely LLM tokenization and tool patterns.
We should reuse the existing trace correlation headers used by the Console tracing team rather than inventing new IDs.
Consider making failure-mode severity configurable so we can run 'smoke' (1k runs) and 'stress' (50k runs) profiles.
progress_updates: 2025-11-12: Spike completed. Prototype generator that emits structured payloads and applies chunk-boundary corruption. Initial scripts live in internal repo: infra/tests/structured-sim
2025-11-15: Proof-of-concept integrated with constrained-decoder binary. Observed two recurring failure signatures: sentinel leakage and KV-cache misalignment at chunk boundaries.
2025-11-18: Built basic telemetry schema and trace propagation; started wiring results into a debug dashboard. Identified need for standardized example format for failing sessions.

2025-11-20: Open questions: (1) how to best surface example payloads in Console without exposing secrets, (2) whether to include live model calls in 'stress' runs for realism vs cost trade-off. Blocking: security review for storing example payloads.
implementation_steps: Finalize simulation spec and canonical failing examples
Implement generator and corruption layer with deterministic seeds for reproducibility
Wire the constrained-decoder invocation and comparison harness
Add tracing headers and metrics emission (histogram + counters)
Create dashboard and regression alert integration with our ticketing pipeline
Run baseline suite and land remediation playbooks for top failure modes
